Attacker-reachable vulnerability
A flaw where input an outside attacker controls reaches a dangerous operation without being neutralized.
Reference set

The 108 curated vulnerabilities, each with its class, source, sink and flow. Results are scored against the frozen snapshot stored in the run manifest; the public findings-attacker-reachable.json files match it except for iguana, which now carries a correction.
Source
Where attacker-controlled input enters the application.
Sink
The dangerous operation the input reaches.
Cross-file flow
A curated flow whose source-to-sink path spans more than one file.
Endpoint rule
The match rule: the right class, and reported locations within two lines of the curated flow's endpoints; for flows of three or more locations, both a source and a sink.
Endpoint-aware configuration
One of the seven configurations scored with the endpoint rule. DeepSec, which reports no endpoint roles, is not one.
Configuration
A complete harness and model combination, such as Claude Code /security-review with Opus 5 at xhigh effort.
Harness
The product around the model: its built-in instructions, pipeline and reporting.
Matched
Credited to a reference vulnerability under the endpoint rule.
Outside the reference set
A finding that matched no reference vulnerability. It is not necessarily wrong.
Macro recall
Recall computed per application and averaged, so each application weighs the same.
Localized recall
DeepSec's metric: class match plus any reported location near any curated flow location.
Classes the built-in review policy excludes or restricts
ReDoS, prototype pollution and open redirect, chosen from Claude Code's /security-review prompt text.
Prompt-swap control
A supplementary run of the same model and effort with the benchmark's default audit prompt in place of /security-review.
